tema: The Bible fell from the sky ready
palavras: the bible fell from the sky
the bible fell from the sky ready
the bible was written by god
a biblia foi escrita por deus
resposta: Myth. The Bible is a collection of dozens of books written by many authors in Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek over a period of about a thousand years. The list of books, the canon, was gradually defined: Athanasius listed the 27 books of the New Testament in 367, and Catholics and Protestants to this day have different lists in the Old Testament.
aprofundar: Inner reading: Saying that a text is inspired is an affirmation of faith, and that is for each person to decide. To say that he fell straight from the sky is a historical claim, and the facts disprove it. Knowing how the Bible was formed does not take away its spiritual value; it takes away the power of the one who says he alone can read. Practice: Read an entire Bible book from cover to cover, asking who wrote it, to whom, and when.
camada3: To ponder: Does your faith depend on a book without history, or can it live up to the truth about how it was made?

palavras: constantine chose the books of the bible
o concilio de niceia escolheu os livros
constantino escolheu os livros da biblia
resposta: A myth, much repeated by critics of religion and popularized by the book The Da Vinci Code. The Council of Nicaea in 325 discussed the dispute with Arius over the nature of Christ, the date of Easter, and norms for the clergy. None of the ancient records and accounts speak of choosing the books of the Bible.
aprofundar: Inside reading: an anti-religious myth remains a myth. Anyone who wants out of the Matrix can't trade an unproven belief for another unproven belief. The real story is even more interesting: the canon has been forming for centuries, in debates between communities. Practice: whenever you hear a shocking revelation, ask: What is the document?
camada3: To reflect: Do you more readily accept lies that confirm what you already believe?

palavras: millions of dead in the inquisition
resposta: Myth. The figure of nine million witches emerged in the eighteenth century, in an unfounded extrapolation, and was repeated for centuries. Historical research estimates that between 40,000 and 60,000 were executed for witchcraft in Europe between 1450 and 1750, mostly by secular and local Catholic and Protestant courts. The Spanish, Portuguese and Roman Inquisitions combined executed a few thousand, not millions.
aprofundar: Inside reading: decreasing crime is lying, and inflating it is lying. Forty thousand people, most of them women, killed by fear and superstition, is already an immense tragedy; it needs no exaggeration to teach. Calculated truth protects against both sides. Practice: When a number seems too big, look for its academic source.
camada3: To reflect: Why does an exaggeration seem stronger than the truth? And what do we lose when we overdo it?

quantum mechanics and the law of attraction
fisica quantica prova a lei da atracao
a fisica quantica prova a manifestacao
mecanica quantica e lei da atracao
resposta: Myth. In physics, the observer is any interaction that records a measurement, like a detector, and not the human mind or desire. No experiment has shown that thoughts change material reality. Using words like quantum, frequency and vibration to sell manifestation is called quantum mysticism.
aprofundar: Inner reading: co-creation, as traditions teach, is an inner practice: intention, emotion and action aligned. She doesn't need a fake physique to be valuable, and she's more honest without it. Practice: When someone uses the word quantum to sell something, ask what experiment shows that.
camada3: To reflect: Why look to science for a guarantee for what only practice can confirm?

palavras: insanity and do the same thing
insanidade e fazer a mesma coisa
resposta: A common myth. The phrase insanity is doing the same thing and expecting different results does not appear in anything Einstein wrote; the earliest known occurrence is from a 1981 text by Narcotics Anonymous. Many other spiritual phrases attributed to Einstein also have no source. An actual quote from him, in a letter to Max Born in 1926: God doesn't throw dice, which he used to criticize quantum physics.
aprofundar: Inner reading: Putting a famous name in a sentence is a form of authority that dispenses with thought, the same mechanism of not touching the anointed. A good idea is worth it; a bad idea doesn't get better with a famous name. Practice: Before sharing a quote, look it up on Wikiquote or Quote Investigator.
camada3: To ponder: Would you agree with the sentence if it had no name underneath it?

resposta: A common myth. The phrase if you want to discover the secrets of the universe, think in terms of energy, frequency and vibration doesn't appear in any of Tesla's writings. Wikiquote classifies it as disputed: there is only the account of a third, Ralph Bergstresser, who said he heard it. There is also no source for the phrase attributed to him about the numbers three, six and nine.
aprofundar: Inside reading: Tesla was a real genius, with patents, engines and alternating current. Turning him into an esoteric prophet with made-up phrases is disrespectful of who he was. Practice: admire people for what they've really done.
camada3: To contemplate: do we need a genius to give permission to our intuition?

tema: We only use 10% of the brain
palavras: we only use 10 percent of our brain
we only use 10% of the brain
resposta: Myth. Imaging shows that virtually all brain regions are functioning, and even during sleep many are active. Injuries in almost any area cause some damage. The brain uses about twenty percent of the body's energy; it would be impossible to keep a ninety percent useless organ.
aprofundar: Inside reading: the myth survives because it promises a hidden power to be unlocked. The truth is more useful: the potential is not in a dormant part, it's in how you use your whole brain, with attention, sleep and practice. Practice: Choose a skill and train 20 minutes a day for a week.
camada3: To contemplate: what power do you hope to gain from outside, that actually depends on training?

tema: In the Middle Ages, they thought the Earth was flat.
palavras: in the middle ages, they thought the earth was flat
flat land in the middle ages
columbus proved that the earth is round
church said the earth was flat
na idade media achavam que a terra era plana
colombo provou que a terra e redonda
igreja dizia que a terra era plana
resposta: Myth. Since ancient Greece, scholars have known that the earth is spherical; Eratosthenes even calculated its circumference, about 240 B.C.E. In the Middle Ages, authors such as Bede and Thomas Aquinas wrote about the round Earth. The idea that everyone believed in a flat Earth until Columbus was popularized in the 19th century.
aprofundar: Inner reading: the myth serves to make us feel superior to the ancients. True humility is recognizing that people in the past also thought well, and that we also have our mistakes that the future will correct. Practice: learn an ancient discovery you didn't know.
camada3: To contemplate: which belief of today will look, five hundred years from now, like our flat Earth?

palavras: jesus was born on christmas day
resposta: The Gospels do not give the date of Jesus' birth; it is unknown. The earliest record of the celebration on December 25 in Rome is in the Chronograph of 354. Whether this date was chosen because of the feast of the Unconquered Sun or by a theological calculation is debated by historians; both explanations have defenders.
aprofundar: Inside reading: both sides exaggerate. Neither is the date a historical fact, nor is Christmas simply a pagan holiday in disguise. What's being celebrated is an idea: the light that rises on the longest night in the northern hemisphere. Practice: This Christmas, celebrate the birth of something new in you.
camada3: To ponder: Does the value of a symbol depend on the date being accurate?

palavras: constantine invented the divinity of jesus
nicene invented the divinity of jesus
constantino inventou a divindade de jesus
niceia inventou a divindade de jesus
resposta: Myth. Christianity existed almost three hundred years before Constantine, and many Christians already called Jesus God long before Nicaea: Ignatius of Antioch, about the year 110, does so in his letters. Constantine legalized Christianity in 313 and convened Nicaea in 325, where most bishops rejected Arius' thesis. He gave imperial power to the Church, and that changed a lot; but he didn't invent it.
aprofundar: Inside reading: What Constantine actually did is more important than the myth: the faith of the persecuted became the religion of the empire. That's where the blending of spirituality and power begins. Practice: always separate the message of a master from the use that power has made of it.
camada3: To ponder: what happens to a message of love when it wins an army?

tema: Fluoride calcifies the pineal gland to block awakening.
palavras: fluoride calcifies the pineal gland to block awakening
resposta: Myth in the form in which it usually circulates. Calcification of the pineal gland is common and increases with age, and a small study from 2001 found accumulated fluoride in it. But there is no evidence that this blocks any spiritual capacity, nor of a plan for it. Fluoride in water, in the doses used, reduces cavities, according to the WHO.
aprofundar: Inner reading: The third eye, in traditions, is a symbol of inner vision, which develops with attention and silence, not with a fluoride-free diet. Seeking awakening in an external enemy is another form of the Matrix. Practice: Ten minutes of silence with your eyes closed is worth more than any detox.
camada3: To ponder: Is it easier to blame a conspiracy than to sit silently every day?

tema: The Christians burned the Library of Alexandria
palavras: who burned the library of alexandria
fire of the library of alexandria
the christians burned the library of alexandria
quem queimou a biblioteca de alexandria
resposta: A simplification that became a myth. The Library of Alexandria did not disappear in a single fire: it declined over the centuries, with budget cuts, the expulsion of scholars in 145 B.C., and a fire in Julius Caesar's war in 48 B.C. In 391 C.E., Christians destroyed the Serapeum, a temple that housed part of a collection; it is not known how many books remained there.
aprofundar: Inside reading: the real story accuses several culprits and above all negligence, which kills knowledge slowly. A single villain is easier to hate, but less teachable. Practice: support a library, a teacher or an open knowledge project.
camada3: To contemplate: What knowledge is dying today, not by fire, but by neglect?

resposta: The vast majority of historians, believers and nonbelievers, accept that Jesus of Nazareth existed: a Jewish preacher from Galilee, baptized by John and crucified under Pontius Pilate. In addition to the Gospels and Paul, he is mentioned by the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus and by the Roman Tacitus. The thesis that he never existed is in the minority. Miracles and the resurrection are already a matter of faith, not history.
aprofundar: Inner reading: calculated truth separates what history holds, existence and crucifixion, from what is belief, miracles. That respects the believer and the skeptic at the same time. Practice: Read the Sermon on the Mount as the words of a real man, and see what they do for you.
camada3: To reflect: What changes in you if Jesus was a real man who said what he said?
